scope: Proposition 5.2 (Transfer to a representing Hamiltonian) of the manuscript “A Coulomb ground-state density without Kohn-Sham ensemble representation” (preprints/A-Coulomb-Ground-State-Density-without-Kohn-Sham-Ensemble-Representation-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 278 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 5a9d714fd656a2c9), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 31. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Assume the hypotheses of Theo- rem 5.1. Let v ∈ L3/2(R3) + L∞(R3) be real and spin independent, and let hv = −∆/2 + v be its spatial one-particle operator, defined by the closed form on H1(R3). Suppose Hv = ∑︁3 i=1(hv ⊗ idC2 )i on H3 has a ground eigenspace supporting an ensemble Γs with nΓs = n. Then Φθ belongs to that ground eigenspace, and there is a real constant eg such that hvg = egg, v = V + eg almost everywhere. (5.12) In particular, V ∈ L3/2(R3) + L∞(R3).
